rationale: A defensible hybrid of the archive's two strongest constructions (dollarized budget-identity inclusion plus own-history benchmarking) rather than a rank splice, though it is close to the boundary of a variant-of-a-variant and the SUB(x, TS_MIN(x,5)) term is non-negative by construction so it partly proxies inventory-ratio volatility rather than a directional build.

This is the archive's leading signal (RequirementWithSelfBenchmarkedOverhang) with TS_RANK swapped for its cardinal analogue — a measurement-scale tweak that, after cross-sectional RANK is applied, will be highly correlated with the original and therefore constitutes a cosmetic variant rather than a substantively different hypothesis.

A legitimate and clearly motivated sample-robustness test of the leading signal that materially raises coverage, but it is a robustness re-run rather than a new mechanism, and the requirement already contains DELTA(invt,1) while the conditioner is also inventory-based, so part of the interaction is self-referential.

The expression matches the hypothesis (high emp/sale relative to own history = overstaffing, high signal, negative expected return), the labor margin is economically distinct from the working-capital margin, and the own-history benchmark plausibly separates it from the published hiring-rate and labor-productivity anomalies.

Internally consistent and completes a coherent three-margin test of the overhang concept, but ppent/sale relative to own history is largely driven by declining sales and thus overlaps existing capacity-utilization and asset-turnover measures, making it the weakest-differentiated of the three template ports.

The sign and construction are correct (low cash-to-current-liabilities by the firm's own five-year standard maps to a high signal value and negative expected returns), and using the own-history benchmark is a genuine diagnosis-driven fix for the earlier cash-buffer conditioners that failed on the FMB slope while also reducing overlap with the published cash-holdings anomaly.
